title: Pinned routing reconciliation with canary splits, tier bursts and cross-region escapes
creator: Ava Chen
description: Problem statement: Pinned-version (session or request affinity) is intended to give a caller a stable model variant during staged rollouts. In practice we've observed three failure modes when pinned affinity interacts with region/tier routing and canary/A-B rollouts: 1) pinned sessions get routed to a region/tier that later lacks the pinned variant (capacity eviction or autoscale), causing live escapes or silent fallback to a lower-quality variant; 2) canary weight shifts don't respect strong session pins, so early cohorts get inconsistent exposures and noisy evaluation signals; 3) burst traffic and tier-based preemption cause pinned sessions to be diverted mid-session, leaking canary assignments and breaking reproducibility. This ticket aims to design and implement a reconciler and heuristics layer that preserves pinned affinity semantics while allowing safe, observable escapes during capacity and tier events.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Deterministic routing precedence documented and implemented: session-version pin (with TTL and escape policy) -> region affinity -> tier preference -> canary weight resolver. 2) New 'pin-escape' window implemented: when pinned variant is unavailable, requests enter a staged escape flow that tries compatible variants by degradation cost, and logs deterministic metrics. 3) Metrics and dashboards exist for pinned-session bounce rate, escape reason distribution, and canary exposure delta with/without pins. 4) E2E integration tests demonstrating stable canary exposures for pinned cohorts and controlled escapes under simulated capacity failures. 5) No regression in percent-tail latency for 95/99 P50 compared to baseline for pinned flows.
implementation_notes:
Design highlights:
- Add pin metadata: (variant_key, created_at, ttl, epoch_id, pin_version) stored in session cookie/authorization context; TTL default 48h, configurable.
- Reconciler: on each request, resolver runs the following steps: 1) check session pin alive -> if variant available and sufficient capacity, route; 2) if unavailable, enter pin-escape window (configurable short window 30s): attempt in-order fallback to 'compatible' variants (architecture-compatibility list from model catalog), preferring same quality class and geo-local variants; 3) if still unavailable, consult canary policy: if cohort assigned to canary but pinned variant missing, probabilistic reassign with cohort-weight-preserving backoff.
- Persistence: pin metadata is ephemeral and kept in the routing state store with TTL and last-seen node vector, replicated to regional caches for low-latency checks. Use existing kv-cache sharding used by serving runtime.
- API flags: expose per-route knobs in Console: pin-ttl, escape-window, escape-policy (degrade-first | geo-fallback-first | strict-fail).
- Backward compatibility: old pins without epoch_id treated as epoch-0 and follow conservative escape policy.
migration_plan: 1) Feature-flag rollout for reconciler logic in staging. 2) Shadow-mode rollout in production: produce logs/metrics but do not change actual routes for 48h. 3) Enable deterministic escapes for a small percentage (1-5%) of traffic tied to non-critical tenants. 4) Gradually increase to 100% after verifying metrics and runbook thresholds. 5) Add UI controls in Console release-2025.03 for pin knobs.
rollout_plan: Phase A (Shadow): 2025-03-11 for 72h collect metrics. Phase B (Controlled): enable for 1% of traffic 2025-03-15 and run for 24h. Phase C (Ramp): 10% -> 50% -> 100% over one week, contingent on alerts. Emergency rollback: kill reconciler feature flag and fall back to previous resolver path.
testing_plan:
- Unit tests for resolver precedence and escape logic with synthetic variant availability matrices.
- Integration tests simulating autoscale eviction and cross-region latency spikes.
- Chaos test: automated node kill in dedicated pools to confirm escape determinism.
- Load test: measure 95/99 latency and token-cost delta under pinned traffic.
- Canary validation: ensure canary metric delta (quality/relevance) is within expected bounds when pins present vs baseline.
open_questions:
- What is the recommended default TTL for short-lived serverless clients vs long-running session users? (propose 48h but open to data)
- Should escape policy prefer same-region lower-quality variant or cross-region same-quality variant when SLO vs cost tradeoffs differ?
- How to record a single canonical reason for escape for downstream billing and SLO attribution?
- Confirm required auditing fields for Private (VPC) deployments to satisfy compliance teams.
